questions.q: Why isn't running a few prompts and checking if the replies "look reasonable" sufficient evaluation?
options: It's actually sufficient for most production use cases
It misses silent regressions and memorization, which a held-out comparison would catch
It takes too long to be practical
It only works for classification tasks
questions.explain: A vibe check doesn't surface the model quietly getting worse at other tasks, or simply memorizing training examples rather than generalizing.

questions.q: What is a held-out evaluation set?
options: The same data used for training, reused for evaluation
A random sample generated by the model itself
The system prompt used during fine-tuning
Labeled examples never used during training, reserved purely for evaluation
questions.explain: Keeping eval data completely separate from training data is what makes the evaluation measure generalization rather than memorization.

questions.q: What specific failure mode does a regression suite on unrelated tasks catch?
options: Slow inference latency
Catastrophic forgetting — the model losing general capability while specializing
Incorrect JSON formatting
API rate limiting
questions.explain: A regression suite checks tasks outside the fine-tuning target specifically to catch whether general capability quietly degraded.

questions.q: Which of these is a warning sign of overfitting in a fine-tuned model?
options: Consistent performance across rewordings of the same prompt
Performance on held-out data matching performance on training data
The model reproducing training examples verbatim on loosely related inputs
A gradually decreasing training loss curve
questions.explain: Verbatim reproduction of training examples on inputs that are only loosely similar is a classic sign the model memorized rather than generalized.

questions.q: What does a smoothly decreasing training loss curve actually confirm?
options: That the model has not overfit
That the fine-tuned task was learned correctly and nothing else broke
That training ran correctly — not that the task was learned well or nothing else broke
That the model will outperform the base model on every task
questions.explain: A loss curve is a training-health check, not a substitute for a held-out evaluation — it confirms the optimization process worked, not that the result is actually good.
